headline.title: Pre-season: cold nights ahead.
headline.text: 23 of the 28 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in White Mountains and Northern Vermont. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Beautiful weekend on tap for the North Country.
Cold front on Monday may bring a few showers but dry weather is largely expected through the upcoming week.

ALY.excerpt: ) High confidence in dry conditions persisting through at least the middle of next week.

GYX.excerpt: High pressure remains in control the weather pattern through next week bringing continued dry conditions and a slight warming trend into Monday.

BUF.excerpt: ) Dry weather is expected the majority of the time through early next week. However, a few rain showers may accompany the passage of a cold front this Monday.

PHI.excerpt:
Elevated tide cycles persist due to Post-Tropical Cyclone Josephine well off the coast, resulting in widespread minor coastal flooding continuing for back bay areas in Ocean County, NJ and Sussex County, DE.
More Frost and freeze impacts expected Saturday night where the growing season continues.

CTP.excerpt: ) Dry forecast holds for the next 6-7 days

RLX.excerpt: ) Dry weather and comfortable afternoon temperatures remain intact well into next week. Areas of dense fog are expected each morning. Patchy frost is also possible each morning through Monday.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Dry, with cold nights.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:22}} to {{t:53}}, mostly dry.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 39).
NWS Burlington forecasters, Saturday 6:38 AM: "Beautiful weekend on tap for the North Country."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and slightly wetter than normal. Wet and mild often means rain below the summits.
